Thanks for the review. It looks like the bug in the `canvas_item_add_line` function, it does not take into account scaling for 1 pixel lines, but does take into account other transformations (for example rotation).

Green and yellow lines are 1 pixel thick, blue and pink lines are 2 pixel thick. Node2D is scaled.

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47700418/130346259-162bb70f-e962-421a-9538-fa5e3da548d5.png)

If I set the border thickness to 2 pixels, then the rectangle is drawn correctly:

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47700418/130346261-9d9bb52a-1324-4f5e-88d7-e3c9c95f587a.png)

I'll take a look at the `canvas_item_add_line` function, but I'm not sure if I can fix this error.

Also I would like to know which option is better.

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47700418/130347717-cca919b6-4873-4934-9b63-5f5db236fed7.png)

I fixed the bug, but the solution is quite hacky. The main drawback is `p_width` rounding.

Also, there is a hack to check the width is 1 due to #51978:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0056acf46fc88757cae9d9f6fe9805f0eec1cd09/servers/rendering/renderer_canvas_cull.cpp#L582-L602

In general, with integer scaling factors, everything is displayed correctly. For non-integer scales, lines can be drawn with different widths due to inaccurate mapping to the pixel grid. But I'm not sure if this problem can be solved at all.

With the current behavior, errors occur even at integer scales and linewidths, especially if the color is translucent.
Does this fix https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/58775?

> Does this fix #58775?

Yes.

```gdscript
draw_rect(Rect2(2, 2, 6, 6), Color.RED)
draw_rect(Rect2(2, 2, 6, 6), Color('yellow', 0.5), false)

draw_rect(Rect2(2, 12, 6, 6), Color.RED)
draw_rect(Rect2(2, 12, 6, 6), Color('yellow', 0.5), false, 2)

draw_rect(Rect2(2, 22, 6, 6), Color.RED)
draw_rect(Rect2(2, 22, 6, 6), Color('yellow', 0.5), false, 3)
```

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47700418/204988049-2b496ced-e5af-4491-a32a-9077d527a284.png)

Nice!

Also, does this fix the bug outlined below on the same issue, with corners being cut off when width is negative, and being repeated twice when height is negative?

On a personal branch I fixed it by getting x and y offsets from multiplying offset by the rect sizes' signs, then using those for drawing. But this PR modifies the logic further so this might not work.

> Also, does this fix the bug outlined below on the same issue, with corners being cut off when width is negative, and being repeated twice when height is negative?

I was unable to reproduce the bug for `rect.x < 0` (as stated in that comment) neither in beta 7 nor in this PR. Negative width/height is handled incorrectly in both cases, but at least there is a message "Rect2 size is negative, this is not supported. Use Rect2.abs() to get a Rect2 with a positive size".

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47700418/205231268-46a10896-4fef-471e-8827-5899f9a2712f.png)

Huh, weird. Maybe width must be >1 for that one? Here's me -

```gdscript
@tool
extends Node2D

func _draw() -> void:
	draw_rect(Rect2(40, 40, -33, -33), Color(0, 1, 0, 0.5), false, 4.0)
	draw_rect(Rect2(56, 40, 33, -33), Color(1, 1, 0, 0.5), false, 4.0)
	draw_rect(Rect2(40, 56, -33, 33), Color(1, 0, 0, 0.5), false, 4.0)
	draw_rect(Rect2(56, 56, 33, 33), Color(0, 1, 0, 0.5), false, 4.0)

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	queue_redraw()
```

![Screenshot from 2022-11-30 17-55-29](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85438892/205303811-eaee1ccb-9140-457b-b2b0-079ad865a67f.png)

No warnings thrown. Or maybe I misunderstood them and this is yet another quirk.

Oh sorry. This warning only appears for `filled = true` for some reason. We need to either add the same warning for `filled = false` or take into account possible negative values. But in any case, a maintainer review is especially needed here, since this code is full of hacks.

Thanks, your script is very helpful. I removed the unnecessary rounding in the case of non-integer `p_width`s, but left the grid snapping for odd `p_width`s and the hack with `p_width <= 1.001` (I believe this is more correct in a practical sense, but I will listen to your opinion if you think differently). Except for this, the rendering is exactly the same as what your script draws (I tested negative values and scaling as well).

However, I'm not entirely sure that the behavior is correct for a negative rectangle width, although it matches your script:

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47700418/205366201-6d05231e-63c4-4156-a11e-b83b453afc91.png)

> but left the grid snapping for odd `p_width`s and the hack with `p_width <= 1.001` (I believe this is more correct in a practical sense, but I will listen to your opinion if you think differently)

Honestly, I kinda ignored how you handle this case. It feels like it needs to finally be addressed properly by allowing the user to choose how the width should be interpreted (then you won't need any special casing in here). Personally I don't think it should ever auto-decide to use line-primitive over the quads. Just because I'm rendering a line with 0.01 width doesn't mean that it should be drawn as an actual line primitive on the GPU. I can have a camera zoomed in close and thus the resulting line can end up visually quite thick. And if I want a thin line regardless of the zoom etc. I should also be able to choose to draw it as such.

Not sure what's the opinion of the rendering maintainers on how this should/can be handled, what needs to be taken into account etc. But yeah, I think it definitely needs to be solved for 4.0.

A possible easy solution would be to make a negative widths be interpreted as "I want a line primitive", positive widths always as quads, and changing the default values for parameters to -1 so it would still not draw quads by default. But again, not sure (yet) if it's fine/acceptable solution.
 
> However, I'm not entirely sure that the behavior is correct for a negative rectangle width although it matches your script

I haven't though about negative values at all when writing that script. So not sure what the behavior in there is and what it should be. As far as I remember in case of rects and negative sizes there are some inconsistencies, in some places they are kinda forbidden / throwing warnings/errors and in other they have well defined behavior (e.g. when drawing texture to a destination rect with negative size it results in flipping the texture on the given axis when it's being drawn).

> Personally I don't think it should ever auto-decide to use line-primitive over the quads. Just because I'm rendering a line with 0.01 width doesn't mean that it should be drawn as an actual line primitive on the GPU.

It's its whole can of worms - there were like three different PRs trying to solve this, but then Chaosus lost interest. Now it's a compat-breaker.

Without this hack, I have no idea how to solve this: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/41239#pullrequestreview-735543356.

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47700418/205378101-3f402258-995a-4554-b15a-73a4c2bcd3f6.png)

I agree that this should be resolved for `draw_line` too. The fact that one pixel wide lines remain thin when scaled is very strange and inconsistent.

> I haven't though about negative values at all when writing that script.

It's funny that we came to the same result.
@kleonc In that case, we'd need to modify some other functions too, like `draw_line()`

> Do you by any chance have a 4.0 project to provide for testing this?

I did not quite understand, this can be tested on any project. Lines that are one pixel wide stay thin when scaled, so it's not surprising that the rectangle splits into 4 lines.

![изображение](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47700418/205386912-42375802-b736-4849-8722-3b371a69b1a9.png)
Superseded by #69851.
Or maybe not and it needs to be rebased on top of #69851?
There are a couple of things in this PR that are not in #69851. I will rebase it soon.

Essentially this PR is now cosmetic, the main bug was fixed in #69851. For negative `width`s, #58775 remains, but there is now a note about it in the docs. @kleonc, is there anything else we can do to reduce the chance of missing corners?

> Essentially this PR is now cosmetic, the main bug was fixed in #69851. For negative `width`s, #58775 remains, but there is now a note about it in the docs. @kleonc, is there anything else we can do to reduce the chance of missing corners?

I think #58775 is not really solvable in a general case. It's not just a matter of obtaining proper final positions of the line endpoints in the coordinate space of the viewport/framebuffer/render target (or whatever you call it) which would be needed to be able to apply a proper offset in that space (small final offset; regardless of the zoom etc.). What we'd also need to know to determine what such offset should be is the exact algorithm used by the Vulkan/OpenGL/etc. for rasterizing the line primitives. And that's problematic, because these can differ between implementations since specifications aren't super strict:
- [OpenGL 3.3 Basic Line Segment Rasterization](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/glspec33.core.pdf#subsection.3.5.1) (for [4.6 it's pretty much the same](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/glspec46.core.pdf#subsection.14.5.1)),
- [Vulkan 1.1 Line Segments Rasterization](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.1/html/chap25.html#primsrast-lines).

So even assuming that rasterization is done according to the diamond exit rule (which is not guaranteed; but maybe it's actually the most common case?:thinking: no idea about that) we would still need to find a way to somehow obtain the final positions of the line endpoints within the fragments' coordinate space (I don't see how we could currently do it). And then we would still need to find a way of how to offset the vertices (probably branching into many different cases) to always produce satisfying fragments. E.g. take a look at the image [from this post](https://stackoverflow.com/a/10341863) and imagine all possible configurations of the vertices (colored dots); and yeah, the rect can end up being transformed in there (so take into consideration rotations or... skewing; yeah, good luck with that :smile:).

**TL;DR**: I don't see us solving it. Would love to be surprised by someone but I don't think it will happen.

For a non-general solution / hacky solution what maybe could be done is adding a method (are a bool param to the current `draw_rect`) which would be supposed to work properly only in a very specific conditions: when the given CanvasItem is not transformed so the offset we would apply to the vertices would actually be equivalent to the offset in the fragments' space. Still it wouldn't be guaranteed to always work because of the loose specifications mentioned previously. Anyway, I'm not convinced that trying to handle such edge case is a good idea.

---

Regarding #35384 I guess it's solved by combination of #69851 + this PR + https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs/pull/6455?

> There's a question whether we should handle rects with negative size properly?

Fixed. `Rect2 rect = p_rect.abs();` is OK?

> Fixed. `Rect2 rect = p_rect.abs();` is OK?

I guess it should be fine, that's a quite cheap call. Potentially could be done just for non-filled rects though.

---

Also does changing how we draw the border for `width >= 0.0` fixes some specific case  (after #69851)?:thinking: 

(left=before; right=this PR)
![a](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9283098/212934734-27ec1af4-1de1-4230-b7cd-f88fa490a3f6.png)

I wonder if there is any specific reason to prefer one over the other.

> I wonder if there is any specific reason to prefer one over the other.

I'm not sure since this PR started quite a while ago and these changes have carried over through all the rebases. I will remove them if they are unnecessary.

> I'm not sure since this PR started quite a while ago and these changes have carried over through all the rebases. I will remove them if they are unnecessary.

To me they do seem like not changing anything (so leaving the changes should be fine too).

> LGTM. Would welcome @clayjohn's opinion on [#41239 (comment)](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/41239#issuecomment-1385618227) before someone will merge this.

I don't think there is a good reason to prefer one behaviour over the other.
Thanks!

issue_context.title: draw_rect is drawn at wrong position. Also size and shape is wrong if filled parapeter is false.
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2 RC 2 Open GLES 3

**OS/device including version:**
Windows 10
Nvidia GTX 1650

**Issue description:**
If filled is set to false, the bottom left pixel appears to be missing, but this is not correct. The size is actually one pixel too wide on both axes. Size and shape works as expected if filled is true. Also all rectangles appear to be drawn at wrong positions. See pictures below.
Related to #32279

Edit: problem is probably related to drawing lines: Drawing a 3 pixel line only shows 2 pixels, omitting the first one. Also horisontal lines are offset 1 pixel down on the y axis. Would probably be a good idea to fix lines first, if rectangles depend on them?

Blue and green are rectangles of 1 by 1 pixel size.
Red and blue are rectangles of 4 by 4 pixel size.
Green and blue have filled = false
Yellow and red have filled = true
![Godot_v3 2-rc2_win64_7h1IAE1juE](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15088582/72761752-46365b00-3bdd-11ea-8060-25a02719554e.png)

filled = false drawn at Vector(1,1) - Shows at position (1,2)
![Godot_v3 2-rc2_win64_qL4B1N6vcg](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15088582/72762090-9cf06480-3bde-11ea-9bfd-8c3bd4432618.png)

filled = true drawn at Vector(1,1) - Shows at position (2,2)
![Godot_v3 2-rc2_win64_TXjYe5qXlT](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15088582/72762098-a4b00900-3bde-11ea-89d7-3a8837a6d99c.png)


**Steps to reproduce:**
Draw a rect with filled, and another without filled at the same size. Compare.

**Minimal reproduction project:**
[Draw_rect.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/4088225/Draw_rect.zip)
comments:
Getting the same missing pixels when tried `draw_line` calls for my rectangles.

(Used a NinePatchRect instead as speed wasn't as issue for my case.)

Will be fixed by a combination of the following PRs:

* #69851
* #41239
* godotengine/godot-docs#6455
